subject: Model comparison beyond the j parameter

messages.author: ef13d6499a420f45
messages.subject: Model comparison beyond the j parameter
parts:
Hello!
I adapted the Psychotria script to compare not only models having the
j parameter or not (i.e., DEC vs. DECj, etc), but also to compare
across the three models implemented in BioGeoBEARS (i.e., DECj vs.
DIVAj).

Because the number of parameters are often the same (e.g., 3 and 3 in
DECj vs. DIVAj), the difference between degrees of freedom is 0, and p
is invariably 0 (indicating significance).

Is this a concern? Does this sort of comparison make sense?

Thanks, Ivan.

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Model comparison beyond the j parameter
parts:
Hi Ivan!

So, the Likelihood Ratio Test and its p-values can only be
used on nested models, where nested means taking a free
parameter and fixing it to the value implied in the model
with fewer parameters.

E.g.,

DEC+J = DEC when j=0

To compare non-nested models, e.g. DEC+J and DIVALIKE+J, use
AIC or AICc, described here:

http://www.brianomeara.info/tutorials/aic

...you can calculate Akaikie weights/relative probabilities
of models. These do not have a formal p-value, but can be
interpreted pretty readily e.g. following Burnham & Anderson
2002:

http://www.unc.edu/courses/2006spring/ecol/145/001/docs/lectures/lecture17.htm

Cheers!
Nick
